items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We called Teddy 'Fess' as so many other orchestra leaders were called. So after hearing my story, Fess told me to go out and get some air for a while and come back later. ... So Fess told me to take the night off. I had seen a trumpet player named Ovie Alston ... Ovie had lived with Billy Taylor who

ctx.x: I had never seen such a beautiful dance hall before, although I had seen some that were as large. The Savoy was long but not too wide, and 2000 people or more could get in the place. I had been told that there were hostesses for men who came alone to dance with. You had to buy a ticket at the end of the week. There was a bar for soft drinks, sandwiches, tables with water service and a cigar, cigarettes, chewing gum and candy stand.

There were two band stands and one of the bands that were playing when I came in was the Fess Williams Orchestra which I had heard about. Fess was dressed in a tuxedo with rhinestones in the lapels and a top hat with the same kind of stones around the band of the hat. The other musicians were dressed in regular tuxedos. I recognised having seen one of the trumpet players when I was younger and had to put/long pants to get into the

Theatres up town in Cincy. I did not know his name but the face I remembered so I asked Cecil who he was and he told me that it was George Temple. George and his brother had been in Cooper's Black and White Show which was a mixed show that I had seen in Cincinnati when I was about 16 years old.
